content:
dana: quick share — ran a shadow-prefetch + speculative decode loop on ozma-lite-30b-4bit this morning. summary below, looking for eyes on methodology and weird regressions.

sujay: nice, can you paste the run command / config?

dana: sure — basic harness:
```
./run_speculative.sh --model ozma-lite-30b-4bit --speculative_ratio 0.6 --shadow_prefetch true --batch 8 --seed 42 --n_runs 3 --eval_sets qa,translation,convqa
```

nina: what were you using for fallback policy? full-token fallback or chunked?

dana: chunked fallback — we fall back to full model decode when speculative path confidence < 0.7 or when KV mismatch count > 3. also a short-circuit on eos probabilities.

matt: quick numbers? latency / quality tradeoff?

dana: p50 token latency down ~1.8x (48ms -> 26ms), p95 down 1.6x. end-to-end latency for QA median 210ms -> 125ms. throughput up ~1.9x on our dedicated A100 pool.

dana: quality: on SQuAD-like QA EM dropped 0.6% absolute, F1 0.4% abs. for translation (WMT subset) BLEU drop ~0.3 pts. convQA [our inhouse eval] shows a small rise in unhelpful answers: +1.1% hallucination flags by auto-detector.

sujay: those are pretty reasonable. did you do A/B with seeds and traffic-split simulation?

dana: yes — each config ran 3x with different seeds (42, 123, 999). A/B simulated 20k queries per arm using our replay harness. CI: bootstrap 95% CI for EM change: [-0.9%, -0.3%].

nina: did quantization cause any bias on certain token classes? e.g., numbers, punctuation?

dana: interestingly yes — rare numeric tokens had slightly lower logit gap, so speculative path mispredicted trailing digits more often. suspect quantized softmax sensitivity. adding a tiny temperature correction on speculative logits reduced digit errors by ~60%.

matt: temperature correction? config snippet?

dana: small patch we tried:
```json
{"speculative_temperature":1.08, "digit_bias_correction":0.02}
```
applied only for tokens matching /\\d+/ in the prefix. helped.

ops-bot: deploy-check: shadow runs ran in namespace ozma-shadow-2026-03-17 — 12 hosts, no OOM.

nina: KV staleness — any signs of degraded context coherence on long convs?

dana: yes for convs > 12 turns we saw a drift where speculative path used older cached KV entries leading to short-term contradiction. mitigation: invalidate prefix cache when fallback_count > 2 within 10 tokens, and add a lookback validation every 8 tokens.

sujay: how about cost delta?

dana: estimated token-cost saving ~44% on inference GPU time for these workloads (because speculative often avoids full-key compute). but because of occasional fallbacks, realized saving is ~36% in production simulation.

matt: do we have a recommended rollout policy? canary % and monitoring hooks?

dana: proposal: canary 5% -> 25% after 6h if: latency p95 improvement hold, EM drop within -1.2% absolute, hallucination auto-flag < +2.0%. add immediate rollback on safety-detect spike > +3% in any 1h window.

nina: one more: eval drift check. we should run an adversarial prompt set tuned for numeric and chronological reasoning to catch regressions early.

dana: agreed — I'll prep a small suite and add to the onboarding checklist.

sujay: LGTM. can you open a short PR with the config + eval seeds and results table? put the temp-correction behind a feature flag.

dana: will do, PR later today. action items: 1) PR w/ config & seeds, 2) add numeric/chron eval set, 3) implement cache invalidation heuristic in runtime, 4) define canary alert thresholds.

matt: thanks — if ops-bot shows any instability overnight ping the oncall. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: oncall is nina from 04:00-12:00 UTC tomorrow.

dana: thanks — noted.
